newsitem.title: SWEDEN: More Swedish households see lower inflation - poll.
newsitem.headline: More Swedish households see lower inflation - poll.

text.p: Swedish households are increasingly expecting a decrease in inflation over the coming year, a survey by pollster SKOP released on Friday showed.

The survey found 12 percent of the 1,000 Swedes polled thought prices would grow at a slower pace in the coming year, an increase by three percentage points from SKOP's last poll in February, the pollster said in a statement.

Households were divided about their living standards over the next 12 months, with 17 percent seeing an improvement, up from 14 percent in February, while 25 percent expected their situation to deteriorate, up from 23 percent.
The number of households expecting the country's economy to improve rose to 23 percent from 21 percent in February while 39 percent saw it worsening, down from 41 percent.
